content.label:
I bought the product expecting it to simultaneously install on my iPad, but no, the iPhone version only works on the phone and the iPad version is double the price. 🙄. I’m not sure if you need one license per device either. 

Next when I imported my calendar, and made a correction on the original calendar, the correction did not trickle through. 

Finally, I note that had I paid extra for the iPad version, synchjng isn’t via iCloud, but their own cloud and so I’ll worried about data security. 

To summarise, a disappointing app that I’ve uninstalled and asked for a refund that’s been denied by the developer so now I’ve approached Apple. 

Beware.

Would love to add tables, images, videos, etc.
As there is a separate app for  iPad; shouldnt there be a function to add written notes & handwriting-recognition?
Also after a word/phrase is made bold/italic, can I not still see the asterisks? An addition of different fonts and colour change of text with maybe custom personalised themes would be great.

title.label: Great app but current version has a big bug

content.label: Love this to-do app, it’s worth the money but the latest version is causing the app to crashing when trying to add a new list item.
A great way to organise and track progression!

title.label: What am I missing? No NLP, no shared lists, no …

content.label:
I tried Things3 a couple of years ago and asked for a refund as it was lacking a few essential functionalities such as natural language, shared lists, etc. So I went to Todoist and later TickTick.

Couple of years later, tried it again and SHOCKED to find nothing seems to have changed. The AppStore blurb still calls it all new except it’s been “all new” for a few years now. Aside from that, still no natural language entry, still no shared lists, no integrations, etc.

I’m summary, nice UI still (if a little dated) but far far away from the features of competitors such as Todoist and TickTick. 

Oh and the whole buying separate apps for different devices is bizarre. I mean I get that it’s a one-time cost but given there has been very little development over the years, I’d happily pay a subscription if it means the team and afford to remain up to date.

title.label: Hopefully it will work better on the second attempt

content.label:
I was hoping it would work better in relation to being able to link projects, re-order priorities and provide better reminders-on balance I think it is overrated but I will try 
again - maybe I didn’t use it properly

title.label: I enjoyed things 3 but I’m leaving

content.label:
There are some glaring functional omissions in this app which I didn’t notice at first although I liked the app when I used it.

However, beware of just how difficult CulturedCode have made it to export your data if you choose to move elsewhere!!

woooooah you guys changed the GAME!!!! Life is so much easier / organised. I’m dyslexic / dyspraxic and so find it very difficult to deal with tons of stuff / goals. This has literally changed my life. Thank you!! ❤️
I already own this on iPad and paid £19.99 for it.  Having to pay an additional £8.99 to also have access on my iPhone is ridiculous.  I have requested a refund.

I’ve used them all over the years: Notational Velocity & nvAlt, Vesper, Clear, Evernote… the last few years I’ve been running Apple Notes & Reminders, but a friend recommended I try Things, and it’s been absolutely everything I’ve ever wanted in a to do app, while having a nigh-on perfect, logical UI.
The way the app structures the todos also maps directly to how my brain likes it. It makes so much sense!
I bought on iOS and my Mac and it’s the best money I’ve ever spent on an app. 💯% thoroughly recommend!
Keep up the great work, devs 💪🏻
It’s great… but expensive. Especially with the MacOS and iPad apps too! I guess you get what pay for but still.

title.label: A meh app that is inflexible

content.label: This is a bit of a meh app. Looks nice, but functionality is lacking. Tag implementation is woeful as it has been from the days of Things 2. No smart lists or saved searches, which is the biggest let down. Add to that no ability to prioritise your tasks (no, a star is not prioritisation) makes this the hardest task manager to manage your tasks. If you don't work by areas a huge chunk of organisation is lost and it's not easy to repurpose. As nice as it looks, I find it hard work to narrow things down and to organise the way that works for me. CulturedCode have one way of managing tasks. If you're not happy doing it their way then you won't like this inflexible app.
I feel on top of everything and this app just guides me through my day every day without much thought on my part. It’s perfect

You need separate apps for iPad although this was the one that came up and easy to purchase. Does not do what I needed so instantly deleted and refund requested. Poor service as I contacted them but heard nothing. Not happy
Love the app, but when are you going to release a collaboration feature?

title.label: If you struggle with the clunkiness of Reminders and Microsoft To Do, look no further!

content.label:
I simply love this App - I have it in iOS and MacOS and it has transformed my handling of my daily / weekly todos.  

Keyboard shortcuts on both MacOS and iOS (iPad with keyboard) are consistent, intuitive and easy to use. 

The ability to forward emails to your to do list is also just brilliant.

Pricey, but Five stars!

title.label: Been waiting for you all my life

content.label: I LOVE this app. I love how easy it is to use, that I can send myself reminders and log them by project if I see something online, the magic plus button, the tags! I could go on! I’ve only been using it for a day and have already transferred my entire life to it! The only issue I can find is that I can’t add a security pin/code to unlock it, would like that to be added in case I lose my phone or for when my daughter pinches it. Other than that - wonderful!
The main icon isn’t great.
Never written a review for an app before- because none has fundamentally changed the way I do stuff like this one. Excellent design and very intuitive. Well done.

I downloaded the iPhone app for £9.99, thinking I could use it across devices. However, I was then asked to pay a further £19.99 for the iPad version, as they are considered separate entities. After I enquired about this, it was explained to me that the iPad version can do more than the iPhone version, so is more expensive. I asked why you can’t pay for the iPad version and get the iPhone version as well, and I didn’t get an answer.

As you can get similar apps for free, that work across devices, I was extremely disappointed that I was being asked to pay £30, and to be honest I felt like I’d been cheated. Apparently, they state in the FAQs that you have to purchase the apps separately. To me, that answer isn’t enough.

Most of the free to do apps even Apple’s   Reminders on iOS has this feature (ability to attach photos or files to your to do list to each entry), Microsoft’s To Do (also free) has it too! Surprised Things doesn’t! Really a deal breaker for me

Things is expensive, for sure, but it’s worth the price. It’s easy to understand and use, there’s no functionality bloat, and the simple, elegant design makes it a pleasure to work with. I wanted a task list app to help me remember ideas and get things done, not nag me and make me anxious – and Things is perfect for that. It’s helpful but never overbearing. It fits intuitively into my work, rather than adding an extra headache or complicated system to memorise. Many thanks to the designers and developers.

I downloaded and paid for 3 things on a recommendation. Wanted to sync across devices. Being asked to pay another £19.99 to use iPad app is nuts. I do t even know if I want to use this app yet and already paid £9.99. Bonkers to be asked to pay 2x again.

title.label: Great app but a few things missing

content.label:
I do love the app. I have had on I phone for a while and I’m currently on a trial run with Mac as I think it’s a great organising tool while I’m working on my business.  My husband also has purchased it on his  iPhone and iPad.

But here’s the problem. 
Even though we have both purchased the app we cannot create a joint list or delegate tasks to one another. This is crazy and seems like such an odd feature to be missing. It’s the only reason why I’m put off buying the Mac version. 

Will this feature ever be added? it would make such a difference and bring so much value to your customers?
Excellent balance of features and simplicity. Its an essential app in my toolbox. A fair price for the iphone app, I hate subscriptions.

I have used Things for years for work and personal and its excellent - reliable and with Things 3, very flexible. It could do with even more flexibility and options however - shame that functionality of flags has been downgraded for the sake of a “ cleaner” look - you can no longer display the actual flag so you can’t see for example a flag denoting “ very urgent” at a glance - you know there’s a flag but you have to go into the actual entry to find out its “ very urgent”.  It could also do with a system of sub headings in my view. Overall - 8/10

Love this app and it’s now a part of my daily life. I do also use it to remind me to complete habits I am trying to form which isn’t much rewarding when you don’t see the complete picture how well you’ve been doing. Although I do understand the purpose of this app is not a habit tracker

title.label: Nothing more than default Reminders app

content.label: This thing does nothing that the default Reminders app doesn’t do.
Absolutely love Things. The best looking task manager by far. The only thing I’d love to see added would be reusable templates. Then it would be five stars for sure. Web access could be useful too.
Tried to use it across two devices but couldn’t get Things Cloud to send me an initiation email. No response from support at weekend. Unimpressed so far.
Just moved my task management over to Things from previously just using the built-in reminders app. Massive improvement, great job!

title.label: Incredible app with the potential to be perfect

content.label:
I love this app, it’s more then a “to-do list” it’s the perfect calendar.

However 

I’d love them to interstate an in app timer function as the app is great for creating a checklist for morning routines, circuit training etc. 

Personally I always give myself how long a task will take and it would be super useful if I could set this time in app rather then having to then open the separate timer application on my phone. 
( this is less of a problem for long tasks but annoying for shorter tasks eg. When using the checklist function for tasks that may only take 1-10 mins)

Overall love the app big well done to the team who developed it 👍

title.label: Fantastic when used for habits alone

content.label: I use this for regular tasks and habits. I initially tried adding one-off tasks as well, but they ended up overloading the process somehow. Used for habits alone, it has transformed my life.

Probably the single most useful app on my phone. Has revolutionised the way I keep track of what I need do in all categories of my life. It might take time to get yourself organised into the app so it works best for you, but now that I have, I am so much more productive because I have planned exactly what I need to do for the day, by setting the date and time with reminder. If I don’t get it done that day, I push it on to another date. Please can the developers add an option to keep an item in a list, even though it has been checked as done?

I don’t normally write reviews and I won’t be too wordy. This app is extremely well designed and the hard work and thought that has gone into it really shows. It has culminated in a very useful task manager which has changed the way I organise my life. Well done developers.

Love the interface and simplicity, but what would make this amazing is if I could actually schedule my day rather than just a list of tasks. To be able to move the tasks and calendar events around on a timeline to easily plan my day..oh how happy I would be...

I’ve used Things for well over 10 years. I think it’s as close to a perfect app as you can get. Its sync is lightening fast between apps. Its core concepts are clear and easy to understand; simple and powerful but without feeling like a glorified front end for a spreadsheet (compare with Omni Focus). It’s user interface is genuinely lovely, it’s just a delight to use.  Best of all it’s very actively developed and just feels like a first class, modern, iOS app.

Style, flow, usability all great! I wish, like so many others, that you can attach docs and photos. Why isn’t this an option?  

Also be good if it had other layouts to choose from such as a Kaban board and progress completion stages or percentage! - and link this to the calendar view. And possibly add task sizing and a RAG status.

So far so good....  with a few more changes, especially the attachment option then it would be 5 Star!

title.label: Feeling organised for the first time in years!

content.label: Brilliant app, I use it to organise home life  on my iPhone (I’m a stay at home mum) and it’s just as good as for work; instinctive, powerful and I can already see the benefits to my productivity one week in.

title.label: 对计划狂来说非常有用

content.label: 明确的目标，是使人上进的永动机，是成功的必经之路，从这个角度来说，Things真的太棒了

I’ve only had the app for a couple of days on my iPhone and iPad and so far I think it’s absolutely brilliant. Very intuitive.

I think it would be even better if there was a  dedicated ‘Tomorrow’ tab underneath ‘Today’ and before ‘Upcoming’ on the home page.

I paid a lot for things on various platforms. Note- despite the wording in their description it does NOT INTEGRATE with google cal or iCal. This means you CANNOT see to dos in your calendars. You can see your calender events in things. I wish they were less covert about this- do not buy this if you want to look in your calender and see what you have to do

Was all good until I upgraded ios and now nothing happens. Deleted and downloaded again, it worked ok until I tried to sync with calendar. I'm guessing it's trying to do something in the background but all I get is a white screen. Money wasted.

This is a fantastic app. It organises all of my todos and reminders. For the iPhone it’s a very good price. For the iPad a little expensive but when we get to the Mac it becomes ridiculous at £48.99. If the developer would sell this at a sensible price I would have copies for all of my Apple devices. But at these prices think again!
Lovely interface and great to use. Migrated from OF but didn’t realise that didn’t support arrangements which is a deal breaker for me........
Things 3 has by far the best design of any task a manger app, yet it is so simple and feature rich too. Nothing beats it.
The absolute Gold Standard of to do apps.
You enjoy making tweaks but still no indicator for repeats on phones. You’ve done it for desktop and laptops so why ever not for phones? Do the basics to get 5 stars.
I could not envisage my life without this App, it is quite simply the best and most convenient workflow App I could imagine. Well done to the developers - you have struck gold!
Been looking for the best digital personal organiser for a long time. It is “3 Things”
